ledger.note: 18 January 1871: the German Empire is founded. 'The empire was founded on 18 January 1871, when the south German states joined the North German Confederation'; William 'was proclaimed Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles'; the new constitution 'took effect on 1 January 1871' and was 'adopted by the Reichstag on 14 April 1871 and proclaimed by the Emperor on 16 April'. The Empire 'consisted of 25 states'. 3 Nov 2026 (fx-53 D02): the January 1871 gain events for the member states were removed; the members live to November 1918 with their own land, so this found takes only land that nobody or the Confederation holds, and a cell a member holds is a conflict the member wins (R3 constituent once data/hierarchy.csv has the row, the size rule until then).

region.text: the Confederation's Prussian core; the member states keep their own land and are constituents of the Empire (they are no longer gained here)

ledger.note: January 1871: the war with the republic goes on under the new Empire. 'In January 1871, these states became part of the German Empire'; Paris 'fell on 28 January 1871, effectively ending the war'.

28 January 1871: truce. 'On 26 January 1871, the Government of National Defence based in Paris negotiated an armistice' and 'On 28 January, a truce was concluded for 21 days'; the war runs 'from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871' (infobox).

1871: German troops hold parts of France as a guarantee. The Treaty of Frankfurt 'required military occupation in parts of France until the indemnity was paid' (5,000,000,000 francs in gold). The page names no departments; the zone is the 452 cells that Cliopatria's 1871-72 German Empire shape holds beyond its 1873 shape (Marne, Aisne, Loiret, Pas-de-Calais, Aube, Meuse, Nord, Somme, Oise and more), which is the war-time zone and wider than the post-treaty garrison.

region.text: the French departments held by German troops, the page names none

ledger.note: 10 May 1871: Alsace-Lorraine passes to Germany. The treaty was 'signed in Frankfurt on 10 May 1871': Alsace except Belfort, most of Moselle, a third of Meurthe and the cantons of Saales and Schirmeck, 1,694 villages and cities, 'about 1,447,000 hectares', 1,597,000 inhabitants; 'the new Imperial Territory (Reichsland)'. The Empire's page calls it 'one imperial territory'.

region.text: Alsace-Lorraine: Bas-Rhin and Haut-Rhin except Belfort, most of Moselle, a third of Meurthe and the cantons of Saales and Schirmeck (about 14,470 km2, 1,597,000 inhabitants)

ledger.note: September 1873: the last German troops leave France. The indemnity was paid faster than agreed and the withdrawal 'occurred in September 1873'.

1884: German New Guinea. The Empire's page: 'by 1884 he had acquired German New Guinea'; the colonies page: 'July 1884 for the northeastern section of New Guinea and neighbouring islands' (the passage is ambiguous between New Guinea and Togoland), 'They also acquired the Northern Solomon Islands' and claimed several Solomon Islands in October 1886. The german-new-guinea dossier gives 3 November 1884. The region is Cliopatria's growth of 1885 over 1873 (825 cells).

region.text: German New Guinea: Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the Northern Solomons

ledger.note: April 1884: the first colony. 'Adolf Luderitz's trading post ... was placed under the protection of the German Empire in April 1884' (South West Africa); Togoland and Kamerun followed in July 1884 and East Africa in February 1885 ('Carl Peters accumulated vast tracts of land'). Cliopatria draws these as the separate row German Africa (1871-1918); the date is the first of the group.

region.text: German South West Africa, Togoland, Kamerun and German East Africa

ledger.note: October 1885: the Marshall Islands. 'In October 1885, the Marshall Islands were also claimed.'
1888: Nauru. 'In 1888, Germany ended the civil war on Nauru and annexed the island.'
1895: concessions at Tientsin and Hankow. 'In 1895, concessions were acquired from Qing China in Hankau and Tientsin.' Cliopatria draws the Tianjin cells from 1898 and drops them in 1917.

November 1897: Jiaozhou Bay. After the Juye Incident of 1 November 1897, 'Kaiser Wilhelm dispatched the East Asia Squadron to occupy Jiaozhou Bay'; the page gives no 1898 lease date (the kiautschou-bay-leased-territory dossier dates the lease to 6 March 1898 and Cliopatria's shape adds Shandong in 1898).

1899: the Carolines, Marianas and Palau. 'Through the German-Spanish Treaty of 1899, Germany acquired the Caroline Islands, Mariana Islands, and Palau in Micronesia' for 17 million gold marks. Cliopatria shows only Pohnpei (2 cells) from 1900.

region.text: the Caroline Islands, the Mariana Islands (except Guam) and Palau

ledger.note: 1899: German Samoa. 'The western Samoan islands, which included Apia ... became a German colony in 1899' under the Tripartite Convention (the german-samoa dossier dates the flag-raising to 1 March 1900).

region.text: the western Samoan islands, Upolu and Savai'i

ledger.note: Late 1914: Germany holds the north-east of France. 'Late 1914: Germany gained military control of important industrial regions in France'; 'The territory occupied by Germany held 64 percent of French pig-iron production'; the Marne (6-12 September 1914) halted the advance. The page names no departments; the region is the French cells in Cliopatria's 1915 German shape (Aisne, Nord, Ardennes and more).

1914: the Russian army invades East Prussia. The Empire's page says only 'a Russian invasion of East Prussia and Austrian Galicia' with no date; the russian-empire dossier dates it to 17 August 1914 and Cliopatria's 1915 German shape lacks 12 Warmian-Masurian cells. Page silent on the year.
1914: the invasion fails. The page links the Battle of Tannenberg without date or description; the russian-empire dossier has it defeated in 1914. Page silent.
1914: Nauru. 'Australia later seized Nauru' (no date on the page; Australia held it until the mandate).
2 August 1914: Germany occupies Luxembourg. 'Luxembourg had been occupied without opposition on 2 August.'

4 August 1914: Germany invades and occupies Belgium. The German armies 'attacked Belgium on 4 August 1914'; the Empire's page has 'Entry into World War I: 1 August 1914' and the Schlieffen Plan 'required violating the official neutrality of Belgium and Luxembourg'. The region is Belgium within Cliopatria's 1915 German shape.

August-September 1914: the Pacific colonies fall. 'Troops from New Zealand invaded German Samoa in August 1914'; 'Australian troops occupied German New Guinea the following month'; 'Japanese troops occupied the German possessions in Micronesia in October 1914' (Marshalls, Carolines, Marianas, Palau). Under the Treaty of Versailles they went to Australia, New Zealand and Japan.

region.text: German Samoa, invaded by New Zealand in August 1914

ledger.note: September 1914: 'Australian troops occupied German New Guinea the following month' (after the invasion of Samoa in August).
October 1914: 'Japanese troops occupied the German possessions in Micronesia in October 1914'.
October 1914: 'Japanese troops occupied the German possessions in Micronesia in October 1914' (the Marshall Islands among them).

November 1914: Jiaozhou Bay. Under the Treaty of Versailles 'Japan gained Kiautschou'; the colonies page gives no date for Japan's seizure (the kiautschou-bay-leased-territory dossier: 7 November 1914).

Autumn 1915: Ober Ost and the Government General of Warsaw. 'Initially, in the autumn of 1915, the entire Ober Ost territory was divided into six provinces' (Courland, Kovno, Vilnius, Suwalki, Grodno, Bialystok); 'The total area was 108,808 km2 ... by the end of 1916'; the Government General of Warsaw was created 'in October 1915'; the page says Ober Ost was 'set up by Kaiser [Wilhelm II] in November 1914'. The region is the growth of Cliopatria's German shape from 1915 to 1916 (Congress Poland, Grodno, Brest, Lithuania; 1,004 cells).

region.text: Ober Ost (Courland, Lithuania, Suwalki, Grodno, Bialystok) and the Government General of Warsaw

ledger.note: 1917: Ober Ost grows. 'In 1917-1918, it was expanded further towards the governorates of Minsk, Livonia, Estonia'. The page names no event for 1917; the region is the growth of Cliopatria's 1917 shape (Volhynia 94 cells, Brest, the islands of Saaremaa and Hiiumaa, the approaches to Riga).

ledger.note: 1917: the Tianjin concession is lost; the colonies page gives no loss date ('The source does not state a loss date or outcome'). Cliopatria's German shape drops the six Tianjin cells in 1917.

March 1917: the Tsar falls. 'In March 1917, the Tsar was ousted from the Russian throne' (Empire page); the Russian Empire ends and the occupied land is that of the Russian Republic, whose events follow. The pairing closes the Russian Empire's part.

ledger.note: March 1917: the same ground is now Russian Republic land under German occupation; Ober Ost was reorganised 'In March 1917 ... into three provinces: Kurland, Litauen, and Bialystok-Grodno'.

ledger.note: February-April 1917: the German armies withdraw to the Hindenburg Line. 'On 25 February the German armies west of the line began Operation Alberich', completed on 5 April; the region is the French cells of Cliopatria's 1916 German shape that the 1917 shape drops (Oise, Somme, Aisne).

region.text: the ground evacuated in Operation Alberich

ledger.note: Spring 1918: the offensive in the west retakes ground. The offensive 'very nearly succeeded in driving the entente armies apart' (page: no date or place); the region is the French cells of Cliopatria's 1918 growth.

region.text: the French ground retaken in the spring offensive

ledger.note: 9 February 1918: the Central Powers sign a peace with Ukraine. 'The Central Powers signed a peace treaty with Ukraine during the night of 8-9 February'; 'German and Austro-Hungarian troops entered Ukraine to prop up the Rada'. The Empire's page: 'All present-day Baltic countries, Belarus and Ukraine were handed to the German occupation authority Ober Ost.' The region is the Ukrainian part of Cliopatria's 1918 growth.

region.text: Ukraine, under the Rada and later the Hetman, propped up by German troops

ledger.note: 18 February 1918: Operation Faustschlag. 'A renewed Central Powers offensive launched on February 18' captured 'large territories in the Baltic region, Belarus, and Ukraine'; the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk of 3 March 1918 made Poland, Estonia, Livonia and Courland German protectorates and Russia 'renounced all territorial claims in Finland'. The region is the non-Ukrainian part of Cliopatria's 1918 growth (Belarus, Crimea, the Baltic). Counterpart (reviewer eu-20-n): Soviet Russia, which signed at Brest-Litovsk (the treaty page names Soviet Russia as the signatory); the russian-republic dossier ends in November 1917.

region.text: Belarus, the Baltic governorates and Crimea, held after Brest-Litovsk

ledger.note: 11 November 1918: the armistice. 'The Armistice of Compiegne was quickly signed, stopping hostilities on the Western Front on 11 November 1918'; the Bolshevik legislature 'annulled the treaty on 13 November 1918' (Brest-Litovsk page). Belgium, Luxembourg (22 November, Luxembourg dossier) and France are cleared within weeks; Ober Ost was 'abandoned after the end of World War I', the withdrawal beginning 'around late 1918 and early 1919'.
11 November 1918: the armistice ends the occupation of Belgium (the page gives no withdrawal date).
November 1918: the occupation of Luxembourg ends with the armistice (22 November 1918 in the luxembourg dossier).

13 November 1918: Brest-Litovsk annulled. 'the Bolshevik legislature (VTsIK) annulled the treaty on 13 November 1918'; the Armistice of 11 November 1918 'had already abrogated the treaty in one clause'. Ober Ost was 'abandoned after the end of World War I', the Germans withdrawing 'around late 1918 and early 1919' (Ober Ost page). The page dates the abrogation, not the German withdrawal. Counterpart (reviewer eu-20-n): Soviet Russia, which signed at Brest-Litovsk (the treaty page names Soviet Russia as the signatory); the russian-republic dossier ends in November 1917.

region.text: Belarus, the Baltic governorates and Crimea

November 1918: the Rada's German backing ends with the armistice and the annulment of the treaty on 13 November 1918.

9 November 1918: the colonies pass out of the Empire's hands. 'Germany quickly lost nearly all colonies abroad'; the exception was German East Africa, where Lettow-Vorbeck's force 'was still active at war's end'. Togoland surrendered on 26 August 1914 and by 1916 Germany had lost most colonies (colonies page); the Treaty of Versailles confiscated the rest.

notes: Seven pages opened against a budget of five: the Treaty of Frankfurt and Western Front pages were opened for the french-third-republic dossier and are cited here so that occupation pairs match; the German Empire page is a broad summary and gives no dated sentence for the 1914-1918 war. Cliopatria draws the Empire from 1871 to 1919, mixing Germany proper with occupied land (the French north-east 1871-73 and 1914-18, Belgium, Luxembourg, Poland, Ober Ost, Ukraine) and colonies; every shape from 1871 to 1918 is adjusted to Germany proper (the 1873 shape) and the rest moves to occupation and vassal events. The 1919 shape is wrong for the Empire (it ended 9 November 1918; the weimar-republic dossier covers 1918-1919). Dossier years differ from Cliopatria's 1871..1919. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D02, 3 Nov 2026): the Empire is drawn as the Holy Roman Empire and the USSR are, a realm whose member states keep their own dossier, land and outline. German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918; the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. So the 19 January 1871 gain events (the 19 member states that have a Cliopatria row in 1870) and the same 19 entries of identity.predecessors were removed: the members live to November 1918 (each dissolves into weimar-republic then; kingdom-of-prussia and kingdom-of-bavaria by fx-45 R121 and fx-46 R122, the other 20 by fx-53 D01), and the gains and R2 would otherwise hand the Empire every member's land. data/hierarchy.csv (rows 1871-1918, constituent) draws the members inside the Empire; the rows for the 22 member dossiers are for the orchestrator (alsace-lorraine, county-of-schaumburg-lippe and principality-of-reuss-greiz have them). The found still names the Confederation's Prussian core; Prussia lives on and holds it, so that part of the claim is a conflict the member wins. Mecklenburg-Strelitz and Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, which never had a gain here, are members too. Mecklenburg-Strelitz, Reuss-Greiz, Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt and Schaumburg-Lippe have no 1870 shape and lie inside other shapes (the dossiers mecklenburg-strelitz, principality-of-reuss-greiz and saxe-coburg-and-gotha exist) and get no gain event here. Counterpart slugs without a dossier: german-marshall-islands, german-nauru, german-micronesia, german-tianjin-concession (colonies; strings only; for a colonies/Pacific batch), russian-republic and ukrainian-people-s-republic exist. Alsace-Lorraine: the Empire gains it from the french-third-republic on 10 May 1871 and the Reichsland of 28 June 1871 is the alsace-lorraine dossier's. Disagreements between pages: the Empire page gives 1 January 1871 for the constitution taking effect and 16 April 1871 for its proclamation, 18 January 1871 for the founding; the colonies page makes the German New Guinea acquisition ambiguous (July 1884; the new-guinea dossier says 3 November 1884). The Solomon cells of 1890-1897 are unsupported beyond the Northern Solomons. Page silent: any Versailles territorial losses (Eupen-Malmedy, North Schleswig, Posen, Hultschin, Memel, Danzig, the Saar: weimar-republic's); the Reichsland's date; the Kingdom of Poland of 1916; the United Baltic Duchy of 5-28 November 1918 (Ober Ost page) is not drawn. Gazetteer: all names resolve.
